title: Exercise and Physical Activity in Parkinson's
content: Regular exercise and physical activity can be an important part of living well with Parkinson's disease. Exercise can support mobility, strength, flexibility, balance and overall wellbeing. Activities may include aerobic exercise such as walking or cycling, strength training, stretching, balance exercises, yoga, tai chi and other activities appropriate to the person's abilities. Exercise plans should be individualized according to mobility, balance, medical conditions and fitness level. A physical therapist or other qualified healthcare professional can help develop an appropriate program, particularly for people with falls, significant balance problems or mobility limitations. Exercise can support symptom management and quality of life but should not be presented as a cure for Parkinson's disease.
